later_revisions.adaptation: Opt-in `query_variants` in retrieval.rank: up to 8 `{text, weight, kind}` variants (text 1-4000 bytes, weight 0-4, kind query, keyword or passage). Repeats of one kind merge case-insensitively and add their weights (capped at 4), as deduplicate_queries does. Each variant ranks the candidates by BM25 (stemmed when `stem` is on) and fuses as arm `lexical_q{i}` at its weight unless `arm_weights` names the arm; a caller's dense ranking for variant i (`rankings.semantic_q{i}`) counts the variant's weight times the semantic arm's. The packet reports each arm's kind, weight, terms and ranked count. Unlike Onyx, the original question keeps its own arms at their usual weights rather than 0.5, and fusion keeps Graphicle's rrf_k (61 unless set) rather than 50. Passage variants follow HyDE (Gao et al., 2022) and query2doc (Wang et al., 2023); rephrasings follow RAG-Fusion; implemented from the papers.

design_adaptations.adaptation: Opt-in `stem`: BM25 terms of all-ASCII-lowercase words pass through the Porter stemmer (including the reference implementation's -bli and -logi departures; words of one or two letters are kept), as in Lucene's and Anserini's English BM25 baselines. Implemented from the published algorithm; no code copied.

resolve_expansion (lines 17-81): user facts extracted from a session or turn join its retrieval key, either merged into the key text (`merge`: fact + ' ' + value), replacing it, or as separate keys resolving to the same id (`separate`).

design_adaptations.adaptation: Opt-in `speaker` in retrieval.rank: a further BM25 ranking over only the lines a chosen speaker wrote (`true` keeps the user's turns; `{keep: [...]}` names up to 8 roles or participant names; `"auto"` picks the side from the question: the assistant's turns when it asks what the assistant said or recommended, no extra arm when it refers to the shared conversation, the user's turns otherwise — this question routing is Graphicle's own design, not LongMemEval's), fused by reciprocal rank beside the full-text arm, so evidence in assistant turns still ranks. A transcript line starts a turn at a `role:` label or, when a kept label is not a role, at a capitalised name of up to three words. Opt-in `key_expansion: "merge"` adds a row's caller-supplied `abstractions` to its lexical text before BM25 (LongMemEval's `merge` resolution of user-fact keys, the key = value + fact join); the speaker and dense arms read the original text.
